en: You are inviting a friend to your birthday party. Write a short message: say which day, what time and where the party is.
fr: Vous invitez un ami à votre fête d'anniversaire. Écrivez un petit message : dites quel jour, à quelle heure et où a lieu la fête.
model_en: Hi Paul! It's my birthday on Saturday. I'm having a party at my house at seven o'clock. There is a cake and music. Can you come? See you on Saturday! Emma
model_fr: Emma invite Paul à sa fête d'anniversaire samedi à 19 h chez elle, avec gâteau et musique, et lui demande s'il peut venir.

en: Introduce yourself to a new pen friend: your name, your age, where you live and what you like.
fr: Présentez-vous à un nouveau correspondant : votre nom, votre âge, où vous habitez et ce que vous aimez.
model_en: Hello! My name is Léa. I am sixteen years old. I live in Lyon, in France. I like music and soccer. I love pizza too! What about you? Write soon! Léa
model_fr: Léa se présente : 16 ans, habite à Lyon, aime la musique, le football et la pizza ; elle demande des nouvelles.

en: Write a postcard to a friend from your vacation: where you are, the weather and what you do every day.
fr: Écrivez une carte postale à un ami pendant vos vacances : où vous êtes, le temps qu'il fait et ce que vous faites chaque jour.

elements.kw: i'm in|i am in|we are in|we're in|here in|beach|mountains|city
every day|i swim|we swim|i go|we go|i visit|we visit|i eat|we eat|i play|we play

model_en: Dear Max, I'm in Nice with my family. The weather is sunny and hot. Every day, we go to the beach and we swim. In the evening, we eat ice cream. It's great! See you soon, Tom
model_fr: Tom écrit de Nice : il fait beau et chaud, chaque jour plage et baignade, glace le soir.

en: Describe your family in a short text: who they are, their age and their job or school.
fr: Décrivez votre famille en quelques lignes : qui ils sont, leur âge, leur métier ou leur école.
model_en: There are four people in my family. My father is forty-five. He is a teacher. My mother is a nurse. My sister, Julie, is ten and she goes to primary school. I love my family.
model_fr: Une famille de quatre : père professeur (45 ans), mère infirmière, petite sœur de 10 ans à l'école primaire.

en: Write an email to a friend about your last weekend: where you went, what you did and how it was.
fr: Écrivez un courriel à un ami sur votre dernier week-end : où vous êtes allé, ce que vous avez fait et comment c'était.

elements.kw: went to|i was in|we were in|visited|stayed

elements.fr: ce que vous avez fait (au passé)

model_en: Hi Sam, how are you? Last weekend I went to the countryside with my cousins. On Saturday we walked in the forest and had a picnic by a lake. On Sunday we visited an old castle. It was really fun, but I was very tired in the evening! Write soon, Nina
model_fr: Nina raconte son week-end à la campagne : promenade, pique-nique, visite d'un château ; c'était super mais fatigant.

en: You can't go to a friend's party. Write a message: apologize, explain why and suggest another day to meet.
fr: Vous ne pouvez pas aller à la fête d'un ami. Écrivez un message : excusez-vous, expliquez pourquoi et proposez un autre jour.

elements.kw: next week|another day|how about|what about|can we meet|monday|tuesday|wednesday|thursday|friday|saturday|sunday

model_en: Hi Jack, thank you for the invitation, but I'm really sorry, I can't come to your party on Friday. I have to work late because my colleague is ill. How about meeting on Sunday afternoon? We could go to the cinema. Have a great party! Ben
model_fr: Ben s'excuse : il doit travailler tard vendredi (collègue malade) ; il propose dimanche après-midi au cinéma.

en: Write a short review of a restaurant or café you like: where it is, what you can eat there and why you recommend it.
fr: Écrivez un court avis sur un restaurant ou un café que vous aimez : où il se trouve, ce qu'on y mange et pourquoi vous le recommandez.
model_en: My favorite café is Bella, on Main Street, near the station. You can eat fresh salads, sandwiches and delicious cakes. The staff are very friendly and the prices are not too high. I recommend it because it's quiet and perfect for reading.
model_fr: Le café Bella, près de la gare : salades, sandwichs, gâteaux ; personnel aimable, prix raisonnables, endroit calme.

en: Describe your town or city: what there is to see and do, what you like and what you don't like about it.
fr: Décrivez votre ville : ce qu'il y a à voir et à faire, ce que vous aimez et ce que vous n'aimez pas.

elements.kw: i like|i love|i enjoy|the best|my favorite|my favourite
i don't like|i do not like|i hate|problem|too much|too many|noisy|expensive|dirty

model_en: I live in Bordeaux, a big city in the southwest of France. There is a beautiful river, old buildings and a lot of shops. I love the markets and the parks. However, I don't like the traffic; there are too many cars in the center.
model_fr: Bordeaux : fleuve, vieux bâtiments, magasins ; l'auteur aime les marchés et les parcs mais pas la circulation.

en: Write an email to the manager of a hotel where you stayed. Your room had several problems. Describe them and say what you would like the hotel to do.
fr: Écrivez un courriel au directeur d'un hôtel où vous avez séjourné. Votre chambre avait plusieurs problèmes. Décrivez-les et dites ce que vous attendez de l'hôtel.

elements.kw: dirty|noisy|broken|didn't work|did not work|cold|no hot water|smell|problem

model_en:
Dear Sir or Madam,
I stayed at your hotel from 12 to 15 May. Unfortunately, my room was very noisy because it was next to the elevator, the shower didn't work properly and the room was not cleaned for two days. I complained to the reception, but nothing was done. I would therefore like a partial refund.
I look forward to hearing from you.
Sincerely,
Claire Martin
model_fr: Réclamation : chambre bruyante, douche défectueuse, ménage non fait ; demande de remboursement partiel ; formules de politesse.

en: Some people think teenagers spend too much time on their phones. Do you agree? Give your opinion with reasons and examples.
fr: Certains pensent que les adolescents passent trop de temps sur leur téléphone. Êtes-vous d'accord ? Donnez votre opinion avec des raisons et des exemples.

elements.kw: i think|in my opinion|i believe|i agree|i disagree|personally
because|since|as a result|that's why|this is why
in conclusion|to conclude|finally|to sum up|all in all

model_en: Nowadays, almost every teenager has a smartphone. In my opinion, many of them spend too much time on it. First, it can affect sleep because they check messages late at night. Second, they may spend less time doing sport or meeting friends. For example, my brother plays games for hours. However, phones are also useful for school. In conclusion, teenagers should learn to use them in moderation.
model_fr: Opinion nuancée : trop de temps d'écran (sommeil, moins de sport), exemple du frère, mais utilité scolaire ; conclusion : modération.

en: Write an article for a school magazine about a person you admire. Explain who they are and why you admire them.
fr: Écrivez un article pour le journal de l'école sur une personne que vous admirez. Expliquez qui elle est et pourquoi vous l'admirez.

elements.kw: is a|was a|my grandmother|my grandfather|my mother|my father|my teacher|famous|singer|scientist|athlete

model_en: The person I admire most is my grandmother. When she was young, she left her village to study medicine, which was unusual for a woman at that time. She worked as a doctor for forty years and helped thousands of people. I admire her because she is brave and generous, and she has always encouraged me to follow my dreams.
model_fr: L'auteur admire sa grand-mère, partie étudier la médecine, médecin pendant 40 ans ; courageuse, généreuse, encourageante.

en: You want to apply for a summer job in a hotel abroad. Write an email to the manager: introduce yourself, describe your experience and skills, and say when you are available.
fr: Vous voulez postuler à un emploi d'été dans un hôtel à l'étranger. Écrivez au responsable : présentez-vous, décrivez votre expérience et vos compétences, dites quand vous êtes disponible.

elements.kw: my name is|i am|i'm a|years old|student

model_en:
Dear Mr. Brown,
I am writing to apply for the summer job advertised on your website. I am a twenty-year-old French student. Last summer, I worked as a waiter in a busy restaurant, so I am used to working in a team and dealing with customers. I speak French, English and some Spanish. I am available from June 15 to August 31.
I look forward to hearing from you.
Sincerely,
Hugo Lambert
model_fr: Candidature : étudiant de 20 ans, expérience de serveur, travail en équipe, trois langues, disponible du 15 juin au 31 août.

en: “Working from home is better than working in an office.” Discuss the advantages and disadvantages and give your own opinion.
fr: « Travailler chez soi vaut mieux que travailler au bureau. » Discutez des avantages et des inconvénients et donnez votre avis.

elements.kw: in my opinion|i believe|personally|i think|from my point of view
in conclusion|to conclude|to sum up|on balance|all in all

model_en:
In recent years, more and more people have started working from home. This trend has clear advantages. Employees save time and money because they do not have to commute, and many say they are more productive without constant interruptions.
On the other hand, working from home can be lonely, and it is often harder to separate professional and private life. Some people also find it difficult to stay motivated without colleagues around them.
In my opinion, the best solution is a hybrid model, combining a few days at home with a few days in the office. On balance, this offers flexibility while keeping the social benefits of the workplace.
model_fr: Avantages (temps, argent, productivité), inconvénients (solitude, frontière vie pro/perso), opinion : modèle hybride.

en: Write a formal letter to your local council about a problem in your neighborhood (traffic, noise, lack of green spaces…). Describe the problem, explain its consequences and suggest solutions.
fr: Écrivez une lettre formelle à votre mairie au sujet d'un problème dans votre quartier (circulation, bruit, manque d'espaces verts…). Décrivez le problème, ses conséquences et proposez des solutions.

elements.kw: dear sir|dear madam|to whom it may concern|yours faithfully|yours sincerely|sincerely|i am writing

model_en:
Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to draw your attention to the heavy traffic in Oak Street, where I have lived for ten years. Since the new shopping center opened, hundreds of cars use the street every hour, especially on weekends.
As a result, the noise is unbearable and it has become dangerous for the many children who walk to the nearby school. Several residents have also complained about the air quality.
I would like to suggest a few solutions: the council could introduce a speed limit of 20 mph, install speed bumps and create a pedestrian crossing near the school.
I look forward to your reply.
Sincerely,
Sophie Durand
model_fr: Lettre à la mairie : circulation dense depuis l'ouverture d'un centre commercial ; bruit, danger pour les enfants ; propositions : limitation de vitesse, ralentisseurs, passage piéton.

en: Write a review of a film or a series you have watched recently. Describe it briefly, say what you liked or disliked and whether you would recommend it.
fr: Écrivez la critique d'un film ou d'une série vue récemment. Décrivez-la brièvement, dites ce que vous avez aimé ou non et si vous la recommandez.

elements.kw: it is about|tells the story|set in|the plot|the main character|follows

model_en:
Last weekend I watched “The Long Road”, a drama set in Canada in the 1950s. It tells the story of a young teacher who moves to a remote village and slowly wins the trust of the locals.
What I liked most was the acting: the main actress is brilliant and the scenes with the children are very moving. The landscapes are also stunning.
However, the film is a little too long and the ending is rather predictable.
Overall, I would recommend it to anyone who enjoys slow, thoughtful films.
model_fr: Critique d'un drame : histoire d'une institutrice dans un village ; points forts (jeu, paysages), faibles (longueur, fin prévisible) ; recommandé.

en: Should university education be free for everyone? Write an essay presenting arguments for and against.
fr: Les études universitaires devraient-elles être gratuites pour tous ? Écrivez un essai présentant des arguments pour et contre.

elements.kw: in conclusion|to conclude|on balance|all things considered|to sum up

model_en:
Whether university should be free is a much-debated question. Supporters argue that free education gives everyone the same opportunities, regardless of their family's income. Moreover, society as a whole benefits from having more skilled workers.
On the other hand, free universities must be paid for through taxes, which places a heavy burden on taxpayers, including those who never go to university. Some also fear that the quality of teaching could fall if budgets are limited.
On balance, I believe university should be free or very cheap for students from low-income families, while others could contribute according to their means.
model_fr: Pour : égalité des chances, bénéfice collectif ; contre : coût pour les contribuables, qualité ; conclusion : gratuité ciblée.

en: “Technology has made us more connected but lonelier than ever.” To what extent do you agree?
fr: « La technologie nous a rendus plus connectés mais plus seuls que jamais. » Dans quelle mesure êtes-vous d'accord ?

elements.kw: however|admittedly|nevertheless|on the other hand|that said|it could be argued
to some extent|to a certain extent|in conclusion|on balance|ultimately

model_en:
Never before have people been able to communicate so easily across distances. Yet a growing body of research suggests that loneliness is on the rise, particularly among young adults. This apparent paradox deserves careful examination.
It could be argued that online interactions are often superficial: scrolling through friends' carefully curated lives may foster comparison rather than genuine connection. Moreover, time spent on screens can replace face-to-face encounters, which are essential to emotional well-being.
Nevertheless, technology itself is not to blame. For isolated people, such as the elderly or those living abroad, video calls and online communities can be a lifeline.
Ultimately, I agree with the statement only to a certain extent: technology amplifies our habits, and whether it connects or isolates us depends on how we use it.
model_fr: Paradoxe connectivité/solitude ; interactions superficielles, comparaison ; mais bénéfices pour les personnes isolées ; accord partiel : tout dépend de l'usage.

en: You recently attended a conference that was badly organized. Write a letter to the organizers detailing the problems, their impact on participants and what you expect from them.
fr: Vous avez récemment assisté à une conférence mal organisée. Écrivez aux organisateurs pour détailler les problèmes, leur impact sur les participants et ce que vous attendez d'eux.

elements.kw: dear|yours sincerely|yours faithfully|sincerely|i am writing to|i would be grateful

model_en:
Dear Organizing Committee,
I am writing to express my disappointment with the International Marketing Conference held on 4 March, for which I paid a registration fee of $450.
Firstly, registration took over an hour, as only one desk was open. Consequently, many participants, including myself, missed the opening keynote. Secondly, two of the afternoon workshops were canceled without notice, and the main hall was so overcrowded that people had to stand at the back. Finally, persistent technical problems with the microphones made several talks almost inaudible.
Given these shortcomings, I would expect at least a partial refund, as well as assurance that measures will be taken for future events.
I would be grateful for a prompt reply.
Sincerely,
Marc Petit
model_fr: Réclamation formelle : attente à l'inscription, ateliers annulés, salle bondée, micros défaillants ; demande de remboursement partiel et d'engagements.

en: Write a report for your company's management on how to reduce the company's environmental impact. Present the current situation, make recommendations and justify them.
fr: Rédigez un rapport pour la direction de votre entreprise sur la réduction de son impact environnemental. Présentez la situation actuelle, faites des recommandations et justifiez-les.

elements.kw: the aim of this report|the purpose of this report|this report|introduction
this would|as a result|which would|in order to|so as to|reduce costs|save

model_en:
Introduction
The aim of this report is to assess our company's environmental impact and to recommend practical measures to reduce it.
Current situation
At present, most of our emissions come from business travel and from heating our poorly insulated offices. In addition, a large amount of paper and plastic is wasted every day.
Recommendations
First, I recommend replacing short business trips with video conferences, which would cut both emissions and travel costs. Second, the offices should be better insulated; although this requires an initial investment, it would significantly reduce energy bills. Finally, single-use plastic cups should be banned and recycling bins installed on every floor.
Conclusion
These measures would improve our environmental record while saving money in the long run.
model_fr: Rapport structuré : émissions dues aux déplacements et au chauffage, gaspillage ; recommandations : visioconférences, isolation, fin du plastique jetable.

en: Some argue that governments should tax unhealthy food to fight obesity. Discuss the arguments and give your view.
fr: Certains estiment que les gouvernements devraient taxer la malbouffe pour lutter contre l'obésité. Discutez des arguments et donnez votre avis.

elements.kw: in my view|i would argue|i believe|personally|on balance

model_en:
Obesity rates have risen sharply in many countries, placing an enormous burden on public health systems. One proposed solution is to tax unhealthy food, as several governments have already done with sugary drinks.
The case for such taxes is persuasive. Evidence suggests that higher prices reduce consumption, and the revenue raised could fund healthcare or subsidize fruit and vegetables.
Critics, however, argue that these taxes are unfair, since they hit low-income households hardest, and that they infringe on personal freedom. They maintain that education is a more effective long-term strategy.
On balance, I would argue that taxation can be useful, provided it is combined with education and with measures making healthy food more affordable.
model_fr: Taxe sur la malbouffe : efficacité et recettes contre injustice sociale et liberté ; avis : utile si combinée à l'éducation et à des aides.

en: “The past is a foreign country: they do things differently there.” Discuss the extent to which we can truly understand people from earlier periods of history.
fr: « Le passé est un pays étranger : on y fait les choses autrement. » Dans quelle mesure pouvons-nous vraiment comprendre les gens des époques passées ?

elements.kw: ultimately|in conclusion|to conclude|in the final analysis

model_en:
L. P. Hartley's celebrated opening line captures a tension at the heart of historical enquiry. If the past is indeed a foreign country, can we ever do more than visit it as tourists?
The obstacles are formidable. People in earlier centuries held beliefs about religion, gender or social hierarchy that may strike us as alien, and we inevitably read their actions through the lens of hindsight. Our sources, moreover, are fragmentary and often reflect the views of a literate elite.
Nonetheless, the gulf is not unbridgeable. Letters and diaries reveal fears, ambitions and affections that are recognizably human. Historians trained to reconstruct context can, at least partially, enter the mental world of their subjects.
Ultimately, understanding the past requires a double movement: acknowledging its strangeness while trusting in a shared humanity. Our comprehension will always be incomplete, but incompleteness is not the same as impossibility.
model_fr: Citation de Hartley ; obstacles (valeurs, rétrospection, sources lacunaires) ; possibilités (lettres, journaux intimes, humanité commune) ; compréhension incomplète mais possible.

en: Write an article for a serious magazine arguing that a common belief or practice in your society deserves to be reconsidered.
fr: Écrivez un article pour un magazine sérieux défendant l'idée qu'une croyance ou une pratique courante de votre société mérite d'être reconsidérée.

elements.kw: widely believed|widely assumed|commonly|it is often assumed|it is assumed|conventional wisdom|most people|we tend to|generally accepted
\?|not only|far from|it is precisely|what is more|rarely

model_en:
It is widely assumed that homework is indispensable to academic success. Parents demand it, schools advertise it, and children dutifully grind through it every evening. Yet on closer inspection, the evidence supporting this ritual is surprisingly thin.
For younger pupils in particular, research has found little correlation between the amount of homework and achievement. What it does reliably produce is stress, family conflict and the erosion of time for play, reading and sleep, activities that are themselves vital to learning.
Far from advocating its abolition, I would argue that homework should be rethought: shorter, purposeful tasks, chosen for their value rather than imposed out of habit. It is precisely because we care about children's education that we ought to question practices we have never thought to examine.
model_fr: Article : les devoirs à la maison, peu d'effets prouvés chez les jeunes élèves, stress et conflits ; plaidoyer pour des devoirs repensés.

en: You are responding formally to a public consultation on a controversial urban development project in your city. Set out your position, address the opposing arguments and propose alternatives.
fr: Vous répondez formellement à une consultation publique sur un projet d'aménagement urbain controversé dans votre ville. Exposez votre position, répondez aux arguments contraires et proposez des alternatives.

elements.kw: i wish to|i strongly|i oppose|i support|my position|i object
proponents|supporters|it has been argued|it is claimed|while i acknowledge
however|nonetheless|this overlooks|fails to|does not take into account
dear|yours faithfully|yours sincerely|sincerely|i am writing in response

model_en:
Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing in response to the public consultation on the proposed redevelopment of Riverside Park into a commercial and residential complex. I wish to register my strong objection to the plan in its current form.
Proponents argue that the scheme would create jobs and help address the housing shortage. While I acknowledge the urgency of both issues, the proposal fails to take into account the park's role as the only substantial green space in a densely populated district. Its loss would have lasting consequences for public health and biodiversity.
I would therefore suggest an alternative: the derelict industrial site on Mill Road, which is of comparable size, could accommodate the housing without sacrificing the park. Part of the park could also be improved with modest investment.
I trust these observations will be given due consideration.
Sincerely,
Anne Leroy
model_fr: Réponse à une consultation : opposition au projet sur un parc ; reconnaissance des besoins (emplois, logement) mais perte du seul espace vert ; alternative : friche industrielle.

en: “Language does not merely describe reality; it shapes it.” Discuss.
fr: « Le langage ne se contente pas de décrire la réalité ; il la façonne. » Discutez.

elements.kw: ultimately|in conclusion|on balance|it would seem|in the final analysis

model_en:
The idea that language shapes thought, often associated with Edward Sapir and Benjamin Lee Whorf, has enjoyed a remarkable revival. In its strong form, it implies that we can only think what our language allows us to say; in its weaker form, that language nudges our perception in subtle ways.
There is evidence for the weaker claim. Speakers of languages with distinct words for light and dark blue distinguish those shades slightly faster. Political euphemisms, such as “collateral damage”, show how vocabulary can soften our perception of violence.
Nevertheless, the strong version overstates the case. People routinely conceive ideas for which they lack words, and translation, however imperfect, remains possible.
Ultimately, it would seem that language is less a prison than a lens: it colors what we see without entirely determining it.
model_fr: Hypothèse Sapir-Whorf : version forte et faible ; exemples (couleurs, euphémismes politiques) ; limites ; conclusion : le langage est une lentille plutôt qu'une prison.
